extraction.name: WikiText
extraction.description: A benchmark dataset for language modeling constructed from Wikipedia articles, released in two sizes: WikiText-2 and WikiText-103.
extraction.creator: Stephen Merity; Caiming Xiong; James Bradbury; Richard Socher
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed by selecting Wikipedia articles rated Good or Featured, extracting their text via the Wikipedia API, and cleaning article content by removing list-heavy sections and extraction artifacts.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw text extracted from Wikipedia articles that met the Good or Featured article criteria.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: List-heavy sections and HTML leakage artifacts were removed; mathematical formulae and LaTeX code were replaced with special formula tokens; low-frequency words were discarded from the vocabulary and out-of-vocabulary words mapped to <unk>.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: After extraction, the text was cleaned, formulae replaced with tokens, and normalization and tokenization were performed using the Moses tokenizer with additional number splitting and minor fixes; the dataset was then formatted to match PTB conventions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Article selection relied on Wikipedia editor-assigned Good or Featured article criteria; these articles had been reviewed by humans for writing quality, factual accuracy, coverage, neutrality, and stability.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to support improved handling of rare words and long-term dependencies in language modeling.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is biased toward Wikipedia articles that are Good or Featured, which are selected for being well written, factually accurate, broad in coverage, neutral, and stable.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: WikiText-2 and WikiText-103 use the same validation and test articles and differ only in vocabulary; words outside the constructed vocabulary are mapped to <unk>.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmark dataset for language modeling, especially for evaluating long-range dependencies, realistic vocabularies, and rare word handling; includes train, validation, and test splits.
